doc.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23

chapter: La Rocca and the jazz-origin dispute
title: Five or six jobs on one Mardi Gras day, and the burned records
summary: Laine recounts the chain of jobs on a Mardi Gras day, and explains his contracts and records were burned after roaches ruined them.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Nine o'clock, I started the Merriors with his ball. We were finished playing that night parade. It was only about, how was they say then, about five blocks we had a walk for the hall.
What kind of a band did you use for the ball? How big a... A brass band. A brass band played that too. Yeah, yeah. About what year was this? About what year? Oh, now I...
About what year? I really, I had a lot of records.

They got so bad in the trunk. When I built this place. When I built this place. I was nothing but roaches. I said, get rid of this. She turned them all out in the yard. I burned them up, I said, oh. You burned it all up then, huh?
I burned it up to just ashes. I burned it.
Well, I didn't blame her because of the drawing roaches and all that sort of stuff, but there was some value for something there.
